questions.question: For a given gas dissolving in a liquid solvent, as temperature increases, the Henry's law constant (\( K_H \)):
options: A) Decreases, which causes solubility of the gas to increase
B) Remains constant because it is a fundamental universal constant
C) Becomes zero at boiling point of the liquid
D) Increases, which causes solubility of the gas to decrease
questions.explanation: From \( P = K_H \chi \), solubility \( \chi = P / K_H \). With increasing temperature, \( K_H \) increases, leading to a decrease in the solubility of the gas.

questions.question: Two non-electrolyte solutions that exert identical osmotic pressure at the same temperature across a semipermeable membrane are termed:
questions.explanation: Solutions having identical osmotic pressures at a given temperature are called isotonic solutions; no net osmosis occurs between them.

questions.question: What is the freezing point depression (\( \Delta T_f \)) of an aqueous solution containing 34.2 g of cane sugar (molar mass = 342 g/mol) dissolved in 1000 g of water? (\( K_f \) of water = 1.86 K kg/mol)
questions.explanation: Moles of cane sugar = 34.2 / 342 = 0.1 mol. Molality \( m = 0.1 / 1.0 = 0.1\text{ mol/kg} \). Depression \( \Delta T_f = K_f m = 1.86 \times 0.1 = 0.186\text{ K} \).

questions.question: At 300 K, pure liquid A has vapour pressure 100 mm Hg and pure liquid B has 200 mm Hg. What is the total vapour pressure of an ideal equimolar solution of A and B?
questions.explanation: In an equimolar solution, \( \chi_A = \chi_B = 0.5 \). Total pressure \( P_{\text{total}} = P_A^\circ \chi_A + P_B^\circ \chi_B = (100 \times 0.5) + (200 \times 0.5) = 50 + 100 = 150\text{ mm Hg} \).

questions.question: Arrange 0.1 M aqueous solutions of the following solutes in order of increasing freezing point depression: (I) Urea, (II) \( \ce{NaCl} \), (III) \( \ce{K2SO4} \), (IV) \( \ce{K3[Fe(CN)6]} \):
questions.explanation: Freezing point depression \( \Delta T_f \propto i \times m \). For complete dissociation, \( i \) values are: Urea (1) < \( \ce{NaCl} \) (2) < \( \ce{K2SO4} \) (3) < \( \ce{K3[Fe(CN)6]} \) (4). Hence \( \text{I} < \text{II} < \text{III} < \text{IV} \).

questions.question: For the Daniell cell \( \ce{Zn | Zn^{2+}(aq) || Cu^{2+}(aq) | Cu} \), the Nernst equation for cell potential at 298 K is:
questions.explanation: The overall cell reaction is \( \ce{Zn(s) + Cu^{2+}(aq) -> Zn^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)} \) involving \( n = 2 \) electrons. The reaction quotient is \( Q = [\ce{Zn^{2+}}]/[\ce{Cu^{2+}}] \).

questions.question: When a discharged lead storage battery is recharged by connecting it to an external electrical source, what reaction occurs at the cathode?
options: B) Reduction of sulphuric acid to sulphur dioxide
C) Evolution of oxygen gas at the plate
D) Reduction of \( \ce{PbSO4} \) to metallic lead (\( \ce{Pb} \))
questions.explanation: Recharging reverses the discharging reactions: at the cathode (negative plate during recharge), \( \ce{PbSO4(s) + 2e^- -> Pb(s) + SO4^{2-}(aq)} \).

questions.sub_topic: Degree of Dissociation from Molar Conductivity
questions.question: The degree of dissociation (\( \alpha \)) of a weak monobasic acid having molar conductivity \( \Lambda_m \) and limiting molar conductivity \( \Lambda_m^\circ \) is given by:
questions.explanation: According to Arrhenius and Kohlrausch theory, for a weak electrolyte, the fraction of molecules dissociated at concentration \( c \) is the ratio \( \alpha = \Lambda_m / \Lambda_m^\circ \).

questions.question: In the protection of iron by galvanization, zinc provides sacrificial cathodic protection because:
options: A) Zinc has a more negative standard reduction potential than iron and oxidizes preferentially
B) Zinc is chemically inert and does not react with air
C) Zinc forms a non-conductive plastic coating over the iron
D) Iron has higher electronegativity and absorbs electrons from zinc
questions.explanation: \( E^\circ_{\ce{Zn^{2+}/Zn}} = -0.76\text{ V} \) while \( E^\circ_{\ce{Fe^{2+}/Fe}} = -0.44\text{ V} \). Being more electropositive, zinc acts as the sacrificial anode and corrodes preferentially, even if the coating is scratched.

questions.question: A steady electric current of 2.0 A is passed through an aqueous \( \ce{CuSO4} \) solution for 965 seconds. What mass of copper is deposited at the cathode? (Atomic mass of Cu = 63.5 g/mol, \( 1\text{ F} = 96,500\text{ C} \))
questions.explanation: Total charge \( Q = I \times t = 2.0\text{ A} \times 965\text{ s} = 1930\text{ C} \). Moles of electrons = 1930 / 96500 = 0.02 mol. Since \( \ce{Cu^{2+} + 2e^- -> Cu} \), moles of Cu = 0.02 / 2 = 0.01 mol. Mass = 0.01 \times 63.5 = 0.635 g.

questions.question: For a zero-order reaction with initial concentration \( [A]_0 \) and rate constant \( k \), the time required for complete consumption of the reactant is:
questions.explanation: From the integrated rate equation \( [A] = [A]_0 - kt \), setting \( [A] = 0 \) gives \( t_{\text{completion}} = [A]_0 / k \).

questions.question: Hydrolysis of sucrose (cane sugar) in acidic medium produces an equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose known as 'invert sugar' because:
options: A) Sucrose inverts into an insoluble starch precipitate
B) The chemical formula of glucose is reversed
C) The optical rotation of the solution changes from dextrorotatory to laevorotatory
D) The reaction consumes light energy and inverts the solution temperature
questions.explanation: Sucrose is dextrorotatory (+66.5°), but on hydrolysis it yields D-glucose (+52.7°) and D-fructose (-92.4°). The net optical rotation of the resulting mixture is laevorotatory (-39.7°), hence 'invert sugar'.

questions.question: For reaction \( \ce{2A + B -> C} \), when [A] is kept constant and [B] is doubled, the rate increases by a factor of 4. When [B] is kept constant and [A] is tripled, the rate triples. What is the rate law?
questions.explanation: Rate \( \propto [B]^y \): \( 2^y = 4 \implies y = 2 \). Rate \( \propto [A]^x \): \( 3^x = 3 \implies x = 1 \). Therefore, \( \text{Rate} = k[A][B]^2 \).

questions.sub_topic: Activation Energy and Enthalpy of Reaction
questions.question: For an exothermic reversible reaction (\( \Delta H < 0 \)), the activation energy of the forward reaction (\( E_{a,f} \)) and backward reaction (\( E_{a,b} \)) are related by:
questions.explanation: For any reversible reaction, \( \Delta H = E_{a,f} - E_{a,b} \). Since \( \Delta H \) is negative for an exothermic reaction, \( E_{a,f} - E_{a,b} < 0 \implies E_{a,f} < E_{a,b} \).

questions.question: A reaction has a temperature coefficient of 2.0. By what factor will the rate of reaction increase if the temperature is raised from 300 K to 340 K?
questions.explanation: Temperature increase is \( 340 - 300 = 40^\circ\text{C} \), which represents 4 increments of 10°C. Rate increase = \( (\text{temperature coefficient})^{\Delta T / 10} = 2^4 = 16 \).

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: What is the ground-state electronic configuration of Gadolinium (\( Z = 64 \))?
questions.explanation: Gadolinium has an extra electron in the 5d orbital (\( 4f^7 5d^1 6s^2 \)) to preserve the thermodynamic stability of a half-filled \( 4f^7 \) subshell.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: In faintly alkaline or neutral solution, potassium permanganate oxidizes iodide ion (\( \ce{I^-} \)) to:
questions.explanation: In alkaline or neutral medium: \( \ce{2MnO4^- + H2O + I^- -> 2MnO2 + 2OH^- + IO3^-} \). (In acidic medium, it oxidizes iodide to \( \ce{I2} \)).

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: Transition metals readily form substitutional alloys (such as brass and bronze) with one another because:
options: A) Their melting points are below room temperature
B) Their atomic radii are very similar (within ~15% of each other)
C) They share identical crystal lattice colors
D) They have completely filled p-orbitals
questions.explanation: According to Hume-Rothery rules, transition metals have similar atomic sizes (differing by less than 15%), allowing atoms of one metal to easily substitute for atoms of another in the crystal lattice.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.sub_topic: Reducing Character of Europium and Ytterbium
questions.question: Divalent ions \( \ce{Eu^{2+}} \) and \( \ce{Yb^{2+}} \) act as strong reducing agents in aqueous solutions because they:
options: A) Readily oxidize to the more stable trivalent state \( \ce{Ln^{3+}} \)
B) Possess completely vacant 4f orbitals in the +2 state
C) Are radioactive isotopes that emit alpha particles
D) Have exceptionally high hydration enthalpies in the +2 state
questions.explanation: The predominant and most stable oxidation state of all lanthanoids in aqueous solution is +3. Therefore, \( \ce{Eu^{2+}} \) and \( \ce{Yb^{2+}} \) readily lose an electron to form \( \ce{Ln^{3+}} \), acting as strong reducing agents.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: In acidic medium, green manganate ion (\( \ce{MnO4^{2-}} \)) undergoes disproportionation to yield:
options: C) Permanganate ion (\( \ce{MnO4^-} \)) and manganese dioxide (\( \ce{MnO2} \))
questions.explanation: In acidic medium, Mn(VI) is unstable and disproportionates: \( \ce{3MnO4^{2-} + 4H^+ -> 2MnO4^- + MnO2 + 2H2O} \), producing purple Mn(VII) and dark brown Mn(IV).

questions.question: Which of the following ligands is ambidentate, capable of coordinating through two different donor atoms?
questions.explanation: \( \ce{SCN^-} \) is an ambidentate ligand: it can coordinate through sulfur (thiocyanato, \( -\ce{SCN} \)) or through nitrogen (isothiocyanato, \( -\ce{NCS} \)).

questions.question: What is the oxidation state of the central cobalt atom in \( [\ce{Co(en)2Cl(NO2)}]\ce{Cl} \)?
questions.explanation: Let oxidation state of Co be \( x \). 'en' is neutral (0), \( \ce{Cl^-} \) is -1, \( \ce{NO2^-} \) is -1, and counter ion \( \ce{Cl^-} \) is -1. Equation: \( x + 0 + (-1) + (-1) + (-1) = 0 \implies x = +3 \).

questions.question: An octahedral complex of formula \( [\ce{Ma3b3}] \) (such as \( [\ce{Co(NH3)3(NO2)3}] \)) exhibits two geometrical isomers called:
options: A) Cis and trans isomers only
B) Dextro and laevo optical antipodes
questions.explanation: When three identical ligands occupy corners of the same triangular face of the octahedron, it is the facial (fac) isomer; when they occupy a meridian line around the metal, it is the meridional (mer) isomer.

questions.sub_topic: Crystal Field Splitting of Co(III) Complexes
questions.question: Why is \( [\ce{CoF6}]^{3-} \) paramagnetic while \( [\ce{Co(NH3)6}]^{3+} \) is diamagnetic, despite both containing \( \ce{Co^{3+}} \) (\( d^6 \))?
options: A) \( \ce{F^-} \) is a weak field ligand (\( \Delta_o < P \)) forming high spin, while \( \ce{NH3} \) is strong field (\( \Delta_o > P \)) causing electron pairing
D) Cobalt in \( [\ce{CoF6}]^{3-} \) has zero d-electrons
questions.explanation: \( \ce{Co^{3+}} \) is \( 3d^6 \). Weak field \( \ce{F^-} \) gives high-spin \( t_{2g}^4\,e_g^2 \) with 4 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic). Strong field \( \ce{NH3} \) gives low-spin \( t_{2g}^6\,e_g^0 \) with 0 unpaired electrons (diamagnetic).

questions.question: The complex \( \text{cis-}[\ce{Pt(NH3)2Cl2}] \) (Cisplatin) acts as a powerful chemotherapy drug by:
options: A) Precipitating serum calcium ions in bone marrow
B) Inhibiting the electron transport chain in erythrocytes
C) Binding to DNA and forming intrastrand cross-links between adjacent guanine bases
D) Alkalinizing the cytoplasm of tumor cells
questions.explanation: Cisplatin enters cancer cells where chloride ligands are displaced by water; the resulting platinum species coordinates to N7 positions of adjacent guanine bases on DNA, causing DNA distortion that triggers apoptosis.

questions.question: Which chloromethane / fluoromethane derivative has the highest experimental dipole moment?
questions.explanation: Dipole moment \( \mu = q \times d \). Although fluorine has higher charge \( q \), the C-Cl bond distance \( d \) is significantly larger, making the product \( q \times d \) largest for \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) (1.86 D vs 1.84 D for \( \ce{CH3F} \)).

questions.question: Hydrolysis of 2-bromo-3-methylbutane in aqueous ethanol produces 2-methylbutan-2-ol as the major product because:
options: A) The reaction proceeds exclusively through an \( \text{S}_{\text{N}}2 \) pathway
B) A secondary carbocation rearranges to a more stable tertiary carbocation via a 1,2-hydride shift
C) Ethanol acts as an oxidizing agent converting secondary alcohol to tertiary alcohol
D) Steric hindrance prevents formation of secondary carbocation
questions.explanation: Loss of \( \ce{Br^-} \) yields secondary \( \ce{(CH3)2CH-C^+H-CH3} \). A 1,2-hydride shift transfers H with its electrons from C3 to C2, generating more stable tertiary \( \ce{(CH3)2C^+-CH2CH3} \).

questions.question: Heating iodobenzene with copper powder in a sealed tube yields biphenyl in the reaction named:
questions.explanation: The coupling of aryl halides (particularly iodobenzene) upon heating with copper powder to form symmetrical diaryls is the Ullmann reaction.

questions.question: Why does 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene (picryl chloride) hydrolyze to 2,4,6-trinitrophenol upon simply warming with warm water, whereas chlorobenzene requires 623 K and 300 atm?
options: A) Three \( -\ce{NO2} \) groups at ortho and para positions strongly stabilize the Meisenheimer anionic intermediate via resonance
B) The nitro groups release electrons to weaken the C-Cl bond
C) Picryl chloride has a tetrahedral sp3 hybridized benzene ring
D) Water becomes a superacid in the presence of nitro groups
questions.explanation: Strong electron-withdrawing \( -\ce{NO2} \) groups at ortho and para positions disperse the negative charge of the carbanion (Meisenheimer complex) through resonance, dramatically increasing reactivity.

questions.question: DDT (p,p'-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) is commercially manufactured by the condensation of chlorobenzene with chloral (\( \ce{CCl3CHO} \)) in the presence of:
questions.explanation: Two molecules of chlorobenzene condense with one molecule of chloral in the presence of concentrated \( \ce{H2SO4} \) (acting as dehydrating agent) to yield the insecticide DDT.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.question: Reaction of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid in the presence of concentrated \( \ce{H2SO4} \) is reversible and is termed:
questions.explanation: Fischer esterification reacts an alcohol with a carboxylic acid in the presence of an acid catalyst (conc \( \ce{H2SO4} \)) to form an ester and water.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.sub_topic: Bromination of Phenol in Non-Polar Solvents
questions.question: When phenol is treated with bromine dissolved in a non-polar solvent like \( \ce{CS2} \) or \( \ce{CHCl3} \) at 273 K, the major product obtained is:
questions.explanation: In non-polar solvents, ionization of phenol to the highly active phenoxide ion is suppressed. Phenol itself undergoes controlled monobromination, yielding p-bromophenol as the major product.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.question: An unknown alcohol \( \ce{C4H10O} \) develops turbidity within 5 minutes when treated with Lucas reagent at room temperature. The alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react immediately; secondary alcohols react in ~5 minutes; primary alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature without heating.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.sub_topic: Mechanism of Ether Formation from Alcohols
questions.question: The preparation of diethyl ether by dehydration of ethanol with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 413 K proceeds via which mechanism?
options: A) \( \text{S}_{\text{N}}1 \) pathway involving a free ethyl carbocation
B) E1 elimination followed by addition of water
C) \( \text{S}_{\text{N}}2 \) bimolecular nucleophilic attack of unprotonated ethanol on protonated ethanol
questions.explanation: Primary alcohols react via \( \text{S}_{\text{N}}2 \): an unprotonated ethanol molecule nucleophilically attacks the \( \ce{-CH2-} \) carbon of protonated ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2-O^+H2} \)) displacing water.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.question: When phenyl acetate is heated with anhydrous aluminium chloride (\( \ce{AlCl3} \)), it rearranges to ortho- and para-hydroxyacetophenone via:
questions.explanation: Heating phenolic esters with Lewis acids like anhydrous \( \ce{AlCl3} \) results in migration of the acyl group to ortho and para positions of the aromatic ring (Fries rearrangement).

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: Aldehydes react with one equivalent of monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry \( \ce{HCl} \) gas to produce:
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic addition of one molecule of alcohol across the carbonyl group gives an alkoxy alcohol known as a hemiacetal; further reaction with a second alcohol molecule yields a full acetal.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: Why is Clemmensen reduction unsuitable for converting 4-oxobutanoic acid to butanoic acid?
options: A) Zinc amalgam does not react with carbonyl compounds
B) Hydrochloric acid oxidizes aldehydes to carbon dioxide
C) The strongly acidic medium (conc. HCl) can cause side reactions or dehydration of acid-sensitive groups
D) Clemmensen reduction works only on cyclic ketones
questions.explanation: Clemmensen reduction requires concentrated \( \ce{HCl} \), making it unsuitable for substrates containing acid-sensitive functional groups (for which the alkaline Wolff-Kishner reduction is preferred).

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: \( \beta \)-Keto carboxylic acids undergo smooth decarboxylation upon mild heating without requiring soda lime because they:
options: B) Are completely insoluble in organic solvents
C) Readily oxidize to carboxylic acid anhydrides
D) Proceed through a cyclic 6-membered hydrogen-bonded transition state
questions.explanation: \( \beta \)-Keto acids form a concerted 6-membered cyclic transition state involving hydrogen bonding between carboxylic acid OH and the \( \beta \)-carbonyl oxygen, expelling \( \ce{CO2} \) smoothly.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: In the mechanism of the Cannizzaro reaction, the rate-determining step is the:
options: A) Transfer of hydride ion (\( \ce{H^-} \)) from the dianionic intermediate to a second aldehyde molecule
B) Initial reversible attack of hydroxide ion on the carbonyl carbon
C) Deprotonation of the carboxylic acid product
D) Protonation of the resulting alkoxide ion
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic addition of \( \ce{OH^-} \) generates an anion or dianion. The slow, rate-determining step is the direct intermolecular transfer of hydride (\( \ce{H^-} \)) to an unreacted aldehyde molecule.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: In the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction, what active intermediate undergoes \( \alpha \)-halogenation?
options: C) Planar carbocation at beta carbon
D) Carbanion generated by sodium hydroxide
questions.explanation: Phosphorus reacts with halogen to form \( \ce{PX3} \), converting the carboxylic acid to acyl halide. The acyl halide tautomerizes to its enol form, which readily reacts with halogen at the \( \alpha \)-position.

questions.sub_topic: Boiling Point Comparison of Isomeric Amines
questions.question: Which of the following isomeric butylamines has the lowest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Tertiary amines lack any hydrogen atom attached to nitrogen and cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other, resulting in the lowest boiling point among isomeric amines.

questions.question: In the carbylamine test for primary amines, the reactive electrophilic intermediate generated in situ is:
questions.explanation: Reaction of chloroform with strong base (\( \ce{KOH} \)) undergoes \( \alpha \)-elimination to generate neutral, electron-deficient dichlorocarbene (\( :\ce{CCl2} \)), which is attacked by the primary amine.

questions.question: Why must the diazotization of aniline with \( \ce{NaNO2} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \) be strictly maintained at 273-278 K (0-5°C)?
options: A) Aniline freezes into an unreactive solid at temperatures above 5°C
B) Sodium nitrite explodes above 278 K
C) Hydrochloric acid vaporizes completely above 0°C
D) At higher temperatures, benzenediazonium chloride decomposes with water to form phenol and nitrogen gas
questions.explanation: Benzenediazonium salts are thermally unstable in aqueous solution. Above 278 K, they hydrolyze rapidly: \( \ce{C6H5N2+Cl- + H2O -> C6H5OH + N2 + HCl} \).

questions.question: In the gas phase, where hydration and steric effects are absent, the basic strength of aliphatic amines follows the order:
questions.explanation: In the gas phase, basicity is governed purely by the electron-donating inductive effect (\( +I \)) of alkyl groups, which stabilizes the conjugate ammonium cation: \( 3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \ce{NH3} \).

questions.question: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with aniline in mildly acidic medium (pH 4-5) to form:
questions.explanation: In mildly acidic solution, aniline remains in free base form rather than being fully protonated, allowing its activated aromatic ring to undergo electrophilic coupling at the para position to form p-aminoazobenzene.

questions.question: Maltose is a reducing disaccharide produced by starch hydrolysis, consisting of two \( \alpha \)-D-glucose units joined by:
questions.explanation: Maltose is composed of two \( \alpha \)-D-glucose molecules linked via a glycosidic bond between C1 of the first unit and C4 of the second unit.

questions.question: Which of the following naturally occurring \( \alpha \)-amino acids is optically inactive?
questions.explanation: Glycine (\( \ce{H2N-CH2-COOH} \)) has two identical hydrogen atoms attached to the \( \alpha \)-carbon atom, making it achiral and optically inactive.

questions.question: Coagulation of egg white upon boiling is an everyday manifestation of:
options: A) Irreversible denaturation of albumin protein
B) Hydrolysis of peptide bonds to free amino acids
C) Conversion of protein into lipid molecules
D) Esterification of amino acid side chains
questions.explanation: Boiling disrupts the hydrogen bonding and secondary/tertiary folded native conformation of ovalbumin, causing uncoiling and irreversible fibrous aggregation (denaturation).

questions.question: Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) contains which transition metal ion at its coordination center and prevents pernicious anemia?
questions.explanation: Cyanocobalamin contains a central cobalt ion in a corrin ring; deficiency causes inadequate maturation of red blood cells leading to pernicious anemia.

questions.question: How does 2-deoxy-D-ribose present in DNA differ structurally from D-ribose present in RNA?
options: A) It contains a 6-carbon hexose ring instead of a 5-carbon furanose ring
B) It contains an additional keto group at C3'
C) It lacks an oxygen atom at the C2' position (has -H instead of -OH)
D) It is the mirror image L-enantiomer of D-ribose
questions.explanation: 2-Deoxy-D-ribose lacks an oxygen atom at the 2' carbon position, carrying a methylene (\( -\ce{CH2}- \)) group at C2' instead of the \( -\ce{CH(OH)}- \) group of ribose.
